premise: Automate what can be automated and put a gate in front of what cannot. Every check below states which side of that line it sits on.

checks.requirement: State "As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases." clearly and prominently on the site.
checks.quote_basis: Operating Agreement section 5 ("Identifying Yourself as an Associate") names the sentence: "You must clearly and prominently state the following ... on your Site ...: As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases." Section 6 (Term and Termination), not section 5, is what deems a violation of section 5 a material breach. Both read on the live page 2026-11-20.
checks.evidence: The exact sentence appears in a strip directly under the masthead on every generated page, and again in the footer. tools/check_site.py fails the build if any page is missing it. Correction 2026-11-20: the material-breach consequence sits in Agreement section 6; the earlier row attributed it to section 5.
checks.gate: none

checks.requirement: Put the disclosure where it is hard to miss, next to the endorsement, not only on an about page or at the end.
checks.quote_basis: "Place it so it's hard to miss... Disclosures are likely to be missed if they appear only on an ABOUT ME or profile page, at the end of posts or videos, or anywhere that requires a person to click MORE."
checks.evidence: Above-the-fold strip under the masthead on all pages, plus a disclosure line immediately above each outbound product button. The footer repeat is supplementary, not the primary disclosure.
checks.gate: none

checks.requirement: Mark every paid or sponsored outbound link with rel="sponsored".
checks.quote_basis: "Mark links that are advertisements or paid placements (commonly called paid links) with the sponsored value."
checks.evidence: Every anchor to an Amazon domain is emitted with rel="sponsored noopener". tools/check_site.py walks all generated HTML and fails if any Amazon link lacks it.
checks.gate: none

checks.requirement: Do not obscure that a link goes to an Amazon Site.
checks.quote_basis: Section 6(w) of the Participation Requirements (Content on your Site) prohibits a link shortening service, button, hyperlink or other ad placement used in a manner that makes it unclear you are linking to an Amazon Site. Read and quoted 2026-11-20; the earlier citation to 2(b) was wrong, because Section 2 ("Links on Your Site") has only subsections (a) and (b).
checks.evidence: The site publishes direct amazon.com/dp/<ASIN> destinations wherever a link is written out. Three buy buttons use a supplied link.amazon short code; each names the product in its text and each card carries the full official listing URL as its source line. Whether the supplied short links are acceptable in the enrolled account is FLG-006 / FLG-026 and is unchanged by this clause check.
checks.gate: Owner action: run the FLG-006 test (one Special Link per product, destination and Associates report confirmed) before scaling. Any change of CTA destination is a decision in SG-13, not an automated edit.
checks.requirement: Do not use a link shortening service, button, hyperlink or other ad placement in a manner that makes it unclear that you are linking to an Amazon Site (Program Policies (S02), Participation Requirements section 6(w)).
checks.quote_basis: Section 6(w), verbatim: "You will not use a link shortening service, button, hyperlink or other ad placement in a manner that makes it unclear that you are linking to an Amazon Site." Located in Participation Requirements section 6, read on the live page 2026-11-20 (the site previously pointed at section 2, which has subsections (a) and (b) only — FLG-020). The related obscuring clause is section 6(v): you may not cloak, hide, spoof or otherwise obscure the URL of the Site containing Special Links such that Amazon cannot reasonably determine where the click came from.
checks.evidence: Verified against the built HTML on 2026-11-20: 25 product buttons ("Check price on Amazon") point to the five supplied link.amazon Special-Link URLs, each marked rel="sponsored noopener" and tagged with data-asin. Each product also has a plain-text source link to https://www.amazon.com/dp/<ASIN> (138 anchors site-wide, rel="sponsored noopener"), labelled with the ASIN and the phrase "official listing". The supplied short links are used as-is; they are not described as invalid or compliant. Their compliance status is unresolved (FLG-006).
checks.gate: Owner action: run the FLG-006 test (one Special Link per product, destination and Associates report confirmed) before scaling. The 6(w) test is about clarity to the reader, so labelling the button is not a substitute for the 2(a)/2(b) tag requirement, which is what the account check settles. Any change of CTA destination is a decision in SG-13, not an automated edit.

checks.requirement: Show price and availability only if Amazon serves that data, or it is obtained through the Product Advertising / Creators API.
checks.quote_basis: Section 2(b) permits displaying price and availability only in those two cases. Re-read on the live page 2026-11-20: "your Site may only show prices and availability if: (a) we serve the link in which that price and availability data are displayed, or (b) you obtain Product pricing and availability data via Creators API or PA API". Section 2(b) adds that a price shown in a comparison format alongside non-Amazon prices must show the lowest "new" price and, where Amazon provides it, the lowest "used" Amazon price.
checks.evidence: The site stores no price and renders none — no price, no discount, no promotional code, no delivery estimate, anywhere. Prices are visible only on the Amazon page after a click. A checker rule fails the build if a currency pattern appears in generated HTML.
checks.gate: none

checks.requirement: Do not make inaccurate, overbroad, deceptive or misleading claims about a product.
checks.quote_basis: Section 2(b): "You must not make inaccurate, overbroad, deceptive or otherwise misleading claims about any Product, an Amazon Site, or any of our policies, promotions, or prices", with the 64 GB / 128 GB example.
checks.evidence: Every published specification is copied from the listing and tagged with a source id and a capture date. Where the listing contradicts itself (P1 capacity units, P2 preset count) both readings are shown and the conflict is named rather than resolved silently.
checks.gate: Human review of editorial prose before each new guide is published. The automated check can prove a claim is cited; it cannot prove the citation supports the claim.

checks.requirement: Do not claim first-hand experience with a product that has not been handled.
checks.quote_basis: "You can't talk about your experience with a product you haven't tried."
checks.evidence: The voice rules ban first-person use claims, durability claims, and first-person testing phrasing. Every product page says plainly that no unit has been handled and that the numbers come from the listing.
checks.gate: Editorial review. See suggestion SG-06: buying one unit per category would let the site make experience claims honestly.

checks.requirement: Affiliate pages must carry original value rather than restating the merchant's listing, or they fall under the thin-affiliation and scaled-content-abuse policies.
checks.quote_basis: Both policies are named explicitly in Google's spam policies.
checks.evidence: Each guide answers a question the listing cannot: how to compare basket against oven form, which specification decides the fit, and how to set up a thermometer against the USDA minimums. The build check enforces a minimum word count and an internal-link requirement on every article.
checks.gate: A human must judge whether the writing is actually useful. Word count is a floor, not a defence.

checks.requirement: Keep the intended ASIN and the observed redirect in separate fields; never merge them.
checks.quote_basis: Section 2(a) requires Special Links to carry the assigned Associates ID; the ASIN is the checkable product identifier.
checks.evidence: Field separation is structural. data/products.json keeps intended_asin, intended_listing_url, confirmation_date and intent_source as flat null fields, and keeps observed_redirect_target, observed_asin and live_recheck_2026_11_20 in separate fields. data/verification.json keeps an intended object and an observed object per product. On 2026-11-20 the earlier 2026-11-19 verification records were found to copy observed ASINs into intended.asin and cite S16 (a NIST page) as the source; those values were blanked and the correction is recorded in that file. No intended ASIN is confirmed by the owner, so no intended value is shown as verified (FLG-001).
checks.gate: Automated: tools/verify_site.py fails if any intended ASIN is filled without an owner-confirmation record, or if an intended source is S16 or any other non-owner reference. Owner action: confirm each link's intended ASIN in the Associates workflow (FLG-001).

checks.requirement: Confirm the tracking ID shopnow047c-20 is present on the Special Links actually published.
checks.quote_basis: Section 2(a): Special Links must use the Associates ID assigned to the account.
checks.evidence: The resolved URLs served to this session carried query parameters but no visible tag= value, so the ID could not be confirmed from outside the account. Nothing about the supplied links is called invalid; the check simply cannot be completed without the Associates dashboard.
checks.gate: Owner action: open SiteStripe or the Associates dashboard and confirm tag=shopnow047c-20 on each of the five links. Tracked as Q-02.

checks.requirement: Links into a product list (search, deal event, department page) require additional original content on the site.
checks.quote_basis: Section 2(b): "Special Links must link to Products (as defined in the Products Statement). When linking to pages with Product lists you must have additional original content on your Site that is relevant to the Special Link. Product lists include search results, events (e.g. Prime Day), or a department homepage (e.g. grocery)."
checks.evidence: The only category link on the site points at the Air Fryers storefront (internal site check, not an external source) and appears inside the comparison guide, which carries its own analysis. No bare list links are published.
checks.gate: Review any future category link before it ships.

checks.requirement: Keep outbound commerce links from crowding out the answer the reader came for.
checks.quote_basis: The people-first content guidance and the page-experience guidance both penalise interruption over substance.
checks.evidence: Each guide opens with the answer, then the reasoning, and only then the product cards. Product cards are capped at two per article by the build.
checks.gate: none

checks.requirement: Record only privacy-preserving events and never associate a tracking sub-tag with an individual user.
checks.quote_basis: Section 2(b): "Under no circumstances may you associate any sub-tag, other ID or reporting provided in connection with the Associates Program with a specific end user of your Site (e.g., you may not dynamically assign sub-tags to users as they arrive on your Site for purposes of monitoring such users' behavior)."
checks.evidence: The outbound counter runs entirely in the visitor's browser, stores a single aggregate count per product in localStorage, and sends nothing. No per-user identifier is created, so no sub-tag could be tied to one. See content/measurement.md.
checks.gate: If a self-hosted endpoint is ever enabled, it must not set cookies and must not store IP addresses — see Q-13.

checks.requirement: Do not assert popularity, trending status or superiority without a dated source.
checks.quote_basis: Self-assessment question: does the content provide insight beyond the obvious, and is the heading free of exaggeration.
checks.evidence: Where the listing itself displays a badge such as Amazon's Choice or a sales figure, it is quoted with the capture date and attributed to the listing. No editorial page claims a product is best-selling, trending or better.
checks.gate: Editorial review of any new superlative.

checks.requirement: Do not display Amazon customer reviews or star ratings, in part or in whole, unless a link to them was obtained through Creators API or PA API (Program Policies (S02), Participation Requirements section 6(t)).
checks.quote_basis: Section 6(t), verbatim: "You will not display or otherwise use any of our customer reviews or star ratings, in part or in whole, on your Site unless you have obtained a link to that customer review or star rating through Creators API or PA API and you comply with the requirements for Creators API and PA API described in the License." Located 2026-11-20; the site had cited this as section 2(t) and, after a section-2-only search, recorded it as not located (FLG-020). Note the permission is a link to the review, not a rating value to print.
checks.evidence: No star rating, rating count or review text appears anywhere on the site. tools/check_site.py rule D10 fails the build on a rendered rating pattern. The 2026-11-19 decision to remove ratings now rests on a located clause rather than a remembered one.
checks.gate: D10-no-ratings (tools/check_site.py).

checks.requirement: No price tracking and no price alerting functionality on the site, unless otherwise agreed by Amazon (Program Policies (S02), Participation Requirements section 6(y)).
checks.quote_basis: Section 6(y), verbatim: "Unless otherwise agreed by Amazon, your Site must not have price tracking and/or price alerting functionality." Located on the live page 2026-11-20.
checks.evidence: The site stores no price and offers no watch, alert, notify-me, back-in-stock or drop-tracking feature, so it is compliant by absence. This row exists to keep it that way: price alerts are the most commonly proposed 'return visitor' feature in affiliate site plans and this one cannot be built without an agreement with Amazon.
checks.gate: Human gate at proposal time. A price-alert or back-in-stock idea must be rejected on this row, not deferred. Recorded as a rejected idea on ideas.html.

checks.requirement: Do not artificially generate clicks or impressions on the site, or create Sessions on an Amazon Site, by way of a robot or software program or otherwise (Program Policies (S02), Participation Requirements section 6(s)).
checks.quote_basis: Section 6(s), verbatim: "You will not artificially generate clicks or impressions on your Site or create Sessions on an Amazon Site, whether by way of a robot or software program or otherwise." Located on the live page 2026-11-20. Section 5 of the Commission Income Statement adds that tags "should only be used to benefit from Amazon Associates commissions" and that claiming the same traffic through another program by manipulating or combining attribution links may end in withheld commissions.
checks.evidence: Nothing on the site clicks its own links. The only outbound automation is a passive listener that counts a real visitor click in that visitor's browser (assets/app.js); it opens no window, prefetches no Amazon URL, and sends nothing to any server. The link checker resolves internal targets only, and the tool that inspects a supplied short link records where it lands without generating a commission-eligible Session; that read is logged as a source observation, not a click event. Any future automated promotion must respect this row: no self-clicking crawler, no synthetic traffic, no click farm, no prefetch of Special Links.
checks.gate: Add a build-time rule if any automation that can reach a URL is introduced: outbound requests to amazon.com from CI must be limited to listing reads and must never carry a tag parameter.

checks.requirement: Do not offer any consideration, reward or incentive for using Special Links; keep Special Links out of Amazon's customer-generated content; email and messaging only where the recipient opted in (Program Policies (S02), Participation Requirements sections 6(g), 6(p) and 4).
checks.quote_basis: Section 6(g): "You will not offer any person or entity any consideration, reward, or incentive (including any money, rebate, discount, points, donation to charity or other organization, or other benefit) for using Special Links." Section 6(p) forbids including Special Links in content placed on an Amazon Site, naming a customer review, forum, Wish List or guide. Section 4 permits Special Links in emails, SMS and direct messaging from your social media Sites only where "such communications are solicited (i.e., opted into by the receiving customer)".
checks.evidence: No giveaway, rebate, cashback, discount or points offer is tied to a link anywhere on the site; nothing is posted to Amazon; no email is sent by the site, and no signup form ships for that reason. The row constrains future plans as much as present state: a lead magnet attached to a newsletter that carries Special Links would need the opt-in to be real, and a 'share to unlock' mechanic would need to avoid the incentive wording.
checks.gate: Review at proposal time. Reader capture is currently an open item (SG-30) precisely because no provider is connected; when one is, the opt-in record is what makes section 4 hold.

checks.requirement: Do not add to, delete from or otherwise alter Program Content, do not frame an Amazon Site, and do not use Program Content to imply endorsement (Program Policies (S02), Participation Requirements sections 6(a), 6(n) and 6(d)).
checks.quote_basis: Section 6(a): "You will not add to, delete from, or otherwise alter any Program Content in any way, including by adding additional information", except resizing an image proportionally or truncating text without materially altering its meaning. Section 6(n) forbids framing an Amazon Site or any part of it within your Site. Section 6(d) forbids using Program Content, including a name or likeness in it, in a way that implies endorsement or sponsorship.
checks.evidence: No Amazon page is embedded or framed, and no Amazon image, banner or API block is displayed: the product cards are typographic label art generated for this site, not Program Content, and the listing text is quoted with attribution rather than pasted as a Program Content block. Whether editorial commentary added next to quoted spec fields is 'adding additional information' to Program Content is a reading the owner should confirm rather than assume, which is why the status is partial and not met.
checks.gate: Keep the rule that Program Content is never rendered as a widget. Any future use of API-supplied images or blocks must be checked against 6(a) before it ships, not after.

checks.requirement: The Site must contain original content, be publicly available, and be identified in the Associates application; third-party material must carry significant commentary, analysis or transformation (Program Policies (S02), Participation Requirements section 1).
checks.quote_basis: Section 1: "Your Site(s) must contain original content and be publicly available via the website address provided in the application. Original content utilizing third-party materials must contain significant commentary, analysis, or transformation to any materials you include." The same section requires the Site to be identified in the application, and lists unsuitable sites, including those carrying false, deceptive, libelous or defamatory materials.
checks.evidence: Original value today is the dated register: every figure traced to a named listing snapshot, both readings published where a listing contradicts itself, and the comparison built from spec fields rather than adjectives. The site is publicly available at the Pages URL. Unresolved: whether the site address is registered in the account (Q-A), and whether volume publishing of generated guides would still meet the 'significant commentary' test. That is the eligibility floor under the automation brief, and it is why the plan gates each guide on a human-verified source row rather than on word count.
checks.gate: One row per guide in the editorial plan: named official source, dated capture, and what the site added that the listing does not contain. A guide that cannot fill those three is not published.

clause_verification: Clause numbers and quoted wording were re-read from the live Program Policies page (page states Updated 2026-04-14) and the Operating Agreement (2025-10-15) on 2026-11-20. Corrections: the customer-ratings rule is Section 6 item (t); URL obscuring is 6(v); the shortener rule is 6(w). Earlier drafts attached those three rules to Section 2, which on that page is titled "Links on Your Site" and has subsections (a) and (b) only. Every clause cited here is recorded with its quotation in data/policy-clause-map.json, and gate D35 fails the release if a clause letter that is not in that map is cited.

citation_correction_2026_11_20.what: Section numbers in the S02 citations were wrong for three clauses, and correct for three others.
citation_correction_2026_11_20.detail: Participation Requirements section 2 has subsections (a) and (b) only. The reviews/ratings, URL-obscuring and link-shortening clauses are sections 6(t), 6(v) and 6(w); price alerts are 6(y); synthetic traffic is 6(s); incentives are 6(g). The price, misleading-claims, sub-tag, product-list and tag-parameter rules really are 2(b), and were correctly cited.
citation_correction_2026_11_20.method: Each clause was read in the page served on 2026-11-20 at https://affiliate-program.amazon.com/help/operating/policies (page header: Updated April 14, 2026), section by section, rather than searched for by section number.
citation_correction_2026_11_20.not_claimed: No view is offered on whether this account is enrolled, whether the tracking ID is valid, or whether the supplied short links comply. Those stay owner-only.
